reason: The whole-app performance audit found that ordinary workspace mode switches were coupled to full project/session initialization. Read-to-Edit and similar navigation cleared the active project, re-read every open-tab manifest, eagerly loaded events/checkpoints/transactions/revision lineage, and statically bundled every document mode behind one workspace chunk. Lease acquisition also began as read-only, creating a false blocked state while ownership was still being negotiated. Recovery P1 keeps the workspace shell and current project mounted across mode changes, hydrates non-current tab manifests in the background, loads History only when opened, lazy-loads individual document modes, and separates acquiring ownership from confirmed read-only state.
affected_workflows: Read / Edit / Pages / Tools mode switching
Workspace tab labels and tab switching
notes: P1 intentionally does not redesign operation concurrency or remove capability gates; those remain assigned to later recovery phases. Regression coverage requires the same workspace DOM shell to survive Read-to-Edit navigation, forbids History/checkpoint/revision reads while History is closed, verifies History reads begin on demand, requires per-mode dynamic imports, and distinguishes lease acquisition from true read-only ownership conflict. Genuine R9 human requalification remains pending.
